Thanks again for the partnership this year. Caroline —

Thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the redlines. Short answer: yes, we can structure a 24-month term that co-terms to 2028-03-31 and support a front-loaded ramp to cover the Sep launch. A few notes up front:

- Co-terming to a customer fiscal date is standard; we'll propose a prorated first invoice to align the start/stop months.
- For the 35% uplift, we recommend a staged commit (Q3: +20%, Q4: +35%) to keep billing predictable while preserving burst capacity.
- Ramp credits: we have an annualized credit model we can apply as a rebate if average utilization exceeds the baseline by >50% in year two — we will map exact thresholds in the SOW.

Looping in Monica and Karthik to draft the amendment and SOW language. I'll follow up with a proposed invoice schedule and draft credit language by EOD tomorrow.

Next steps: 1) Confirm quarterly invoice cadence with procurement, 2) Monica to prepare amendment, 3) Karthik to confirm pricing for staged commit.

Jonas Weber

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: draft amendment + amortization options

Jonas / Karthik —

Drafted two lightweight approaches for the amendment (attached):

A) Rolling-start 24-month term that begins on signature date, co-terms to 2028-03-31 via prorated first/last month. Invoices issued quarterly in arrears, true-ups monthly. Credit: annual rebate equal to 10% of quarterly overage spend applied as a credit on next invoice if year-two average utilization > 50% above baseline.

B) Fixed fiscal term (2026-04-01 to 2028-03-31) with front-loaded commit buckets for Q3 and Q4. Invoices are quarterly based on committed buckets with monthly true-up. Credit: upfront prepaid credit that reduces invoice burn rate if overage thresholds hit.

I've included line-item math in the spreadsheet for both. Key questions for pricing: which model keeps unit economics flat if StorLytics accelerates consumption post-launch? Karthik, can you validate the margin impact for option B (prepaid credit)?

Also tagging Lauren for procurement cadence: Lauren, customer prefers quarterly invoices with procurement sign-off mid-April — will that timeline work for bill-of-sale/PO?

—Monica
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOW_StorLytics_Q3-Q5.xlsx (contains amortization tables)
